patch_description: The current code spreads partitions across k parallel paths with a round-robin scheme, which increases total cost: later partitions are pushed onto more expensive routes even though the cost model charges for data already-delivered trunks only once. The key insight is that edge reuse should be rewarded, not penalized: once a trunk (src, dst) has been paid for by an earlier destination/partition, sending subsequent partitions over it is essentially free. So we (1) drop the load-spreading round-robin and instead route every partition on its cheapest path computed with reuse-discounted edge weights, and (2) add an outer refinement loop that re-runs the routing pass with `used_edges` carried over from the previous pass — iterated discounting typically converges to better shared trunks in 2–3 passes at trivial compute cost. This reduces redundant transfers and consolidates traffic onto already-paid routes, directly minimizing total transfer cost.
